name: Job handler
purpose: Execute the work for a single job, with no knowledge of how that job was delivered.
responsibilities: Implement the unit of work for one job type
Be idempotent — the same job may arrive more than once
Classify failures as retryable or terminal, explicitly
Emit a structured outcome that the consumer can act on
Enforce its own timeout rather than relying on the broker's visibility window
restrictions: Must NOT know which broker delivered the job
Must NOT acknowledge, negatively acknowledge or dead-letter — that is the consumer's job
Must NOT schedule or enqueue its own retries
Must NOT assume exactly-once delivery, or that it is the only handler running
Must NOT import a queue client library

interface.errorHandling: Throw a typed error carrying retryability. A bare throw is treated as retryable, which is the safe default but a poor one to rely on.

idempotency.description: Derive a stable idempotency key from the job payload, not from the delivery. Check-and-set before doing side-effectful work so a redelivery is a cheap no-op.

failureClassification.description: A validation failure or a 4xx from a dependency is terminal — retrying will not help. A timeout, a 5xx or a lock conflict is retryable. Say which; do not make the consumer guess.

agentHints: This is the layer worth unit-testing. It should be callable with a plain object and no infrastructure.
Write the idempotency check before the side effect, not after.
If the handler needs to know the retry count to make a decision, take it as a parameter — do not reach for the broker.
Long-running work belongs behind a checkpoint, not inside one job that exceeds the visibility timeout.
